key_insight: DFT predicts stronger vacancy association in CrN than TiN, with compact mixed-vacancy clusters remaining favourable at CrN surfaces but becoming unfavourable at TiN surfaces.
engineering_relevance: Material choice, growth chemical potentials, and proximity to surfaces can influence vacancy populations and clustering in TiN and CrN coatings.
method: DFT calculations of native vacancies in bulk and at rocksalt (001) surfaces.
Formation energies evaluated across phase-stability-constrained chemical potentials.
Association energies referenced to isolated vacancies, using preferred depths for surface comparisons.
evidence_signal: For compact clusters containing two metal and two nitrogen vacancies, association energies change from +0.217 to −0.346 eV per vacancy from bulk to surface in TiN, versus +1.188 to +0.431 in CrN; positive values favour association.
watch_item: The reported DFT energetics do not establish finite-temperature vacancy populations or clustering kinetics under coating-growth conditions.
paper_title: Native vacancy energetics and association in TiN and CrN: chemical potential dependence, clustering, and surface effects
